fields.features_heading: What a Waiver Signed at the Door Holds
fields.features_subheading: Six parts that get a signature from every student, including the one who walks in two minutes before class.
fields.feature_1:
Made for a phone at the front desk

Students open the waiver from a link or a QR code and finish it standing in the lobby. The app can show one question per screen, so long clauses stay readable on a small display.
fields.feature_2:
Injury notes the teacher sees first

Ask each student to describe any injury or recent surgery in their own words. The app emails that note to the teacher of their next class, who reads it before the first pose.
fields.feature_3:
One plain question about touch

Ask whether the teacher may give hands-on assists, answered yes or no. The answer stays on the student's record, and a student who changes their mind updates it next visit.
fields.feature_4:
A signature saved with its wording

Each student signs with a finger at the end of the waiver. The app captures the signature with the date, the time, and the waiver version that the student read and agreed to.
fields.feature_5:
Rosters that show who still owes one

Every class list carries a Signed or Not signed tag beside each name. Teachers check it on a phone as people unroll their mats, without paging through a binder of paper.
fields.feature_6:
Waivers in a database you own

Signed waivers land in a database you own, searchable by student name. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host it where the studio books classes.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Studios Get Every Student Signed
fields.tab_content_1:
From the door code to Signed on the roster

Juniper Room Yoga gets a few walk-ins before every evening class. A QR code taped by the front desk opens the waiver. Ingrid Sarafian is there for her first class. She scans it and signs on her phone while she pulls off her shoes. On the 6:00 PM vinyasa roster, her name now reads Signed.
fields.tab_content_2:
A no to assists, printed beside her name

Briarwood Yoga asks every student one question before their first class: may the teacher give hands-on assists? Pema Delacorte answered no. Thessaly Rourke, who teaches the Thursday 7:30 AM flow, sees a No assists tag beside Pema's name on the roster and cues her with words instead.
fields.tab_content_3:
With no signature, the waiver arrives before the link

Halcyon Street Yoga streams a Sunday 9:00 AM class for students at home. The livestream link goes out by email only to registrants who have signed. Corbin Achterberg registered on Saturday night and skipped the waiver, so his first email holds the waiver link. He signs from it, and the class link follows right after.
fields.tab_content_4:
18 aerial students, one new version to sign

Lumen Loft added silks classes this fall, and its attorney wrote an aerial clause that became waiver version 3. The 18 aerial students who signed version 2 are asked to sign version 3 the next time they book an aerial class. Esme Valcourt signs it before her Tuesday silks spot is confirmed.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Yoga Waiver Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a yoga waiver form that every student signs before class, with the release wording checked by an attorney.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down every class you run
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask what the teacher needs to know
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Send the draft to an attorney
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the classes the studio teaches, such as heated flow or aerial silks. A class with its own risks gets its own clause, and students sign only the sections for the classes they book.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Add a free-text question for injuries or recent surgery, and a yes or no on hands-on assists. Keep that section short, because a teacher reads it minutes before class starts.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Have a local attorney read the release wording before any student signs it. Yoga Journal's advice is that anyone interested in consent forms and waivers should consult an attorney.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Print a QR code for the front desk and put the waiver link in every booking confirmation. Livestream registrants get it in an email that arrives before the class link.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the clauses, the questions, and the signing rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the yoga waiver form, the database behind it, and a roster view for teachers. Change any of it later in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Number each version of the waiver
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give the waiver a version number and save it with every signature. When the wording changes, students on the older version sign the new one at their next booking.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Sign it yourself from a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Scan the QR code, sign as a test student, and open the roster. Check that the test name reads Signed and that a no to assists shows up beside it.

faq_plan.q: What is a yoga waiver form?
faq_plan.a: A yoga waiver form is the document a student reads and signs before practicing at a studio. It describes the physical risks of class, asks the student to accept them, and can include a release of liability for the studio and its teachers. Yoga Journal lists putting the student on notice of the risks associated with yoga as one reason to have each student sign.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a yoga waiver form?
faq_plan.a: List your classes and the questions a teacher needs answered, then have an attorney check the release wording. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form, the database that holds signed waivers, and a roster view that shows who has signed.

faq_plan.q: Can you provide some examples of yoga waiver forms?
faq_plan.ref: Can you provide some examples of yoga waiver forms?

prov.original: Can you provide some examples of yoga waiver forms?

faq_plan.a: Yes. Studio waivers share a few clauses and word them differently. Serene Yoga Studio's has the student state that yoga is not a substitute for medical attention. YYOGA's asks the student to attest to having no medical or emotional condition that would prevent them from practicing safely. Other yoga waiver forms add an aerial clause.

faq_plan.q: What should a yoga waiver form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with contact details, the risks of class, the release wording, and a dated signature. Then add what a general liability waiver form leaves out: injury notes and the assists question. Yoga Journal says a waiver allows prospective students the opportunity to consider their health and whether yoga is right for them.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free yoga waiver form that students sign online?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing, so a free yoga waiver form can go live the same day. Students scan a QR code at the desk and sign on their own phones. A yoga waiver form pdf from another studio's site shows sample wording to take to your attorney, but each copy still gets printed and filed by hand.

faq_plan.q: How often should students sign a new yoga waiver form?
faq_plan.a: Once when they register, and again whenever the wording changes. Yoga Journal says that, ideally, signing should be a routine part of registering a new student. After that, save a version number with each signature. When a new clause is added, ask students on the older version to sign at their next booking instead of asking everyone before every class.

faq_plan.q: Can one yoga waiver form cover both mat and aerial classes?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the form shows each class's clause only to students who book that class. Keep the general release for everyone, then add a section for aerial rigs that appears when a student books silks or hammock. A salon waiver form works the same way, with sections that depend on the service booked.

faq_plan.q: Where should a studio keep each signed yoga waiver form?
faq_plan.a: Keep them in one place you can search by student name, with the date and the waiver version beside each signature. A box of paper sheets is slow to search when a student asks what they signed. On a form built with Emergent, each signed waiver lands in a database you own, and on paid plans you can export the full code.

faq_plan.q: Can students sign a yoga waiver form on their phone before class?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A QR code at the front desk or a link in the booking email opens the waiver on the student's own phone, and they sign with a finger. An app built with Emergent can capture the e-signature with the date and time, and the roster shows the teacher who has signed. Whether an e-signed waiver holds up is a question for your attorney.

faq_plan.q: Should a yoga waiver form ask about hands-on assists?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if your teachers give assists. Yoga Journal draws the line this way: a consent form or provision could cover details such as consenting to being touched, whereas a waiver of liability could potentially release a teacher from liability related to her touch. Asking on the waiver keeps one form per student.

plan.angle: The top 10 is studio waiver text (YYOGA, Serene Yoga Studio, Auckland Yoga Academy, Marcia Sharp), a Yoga Journal piece on whether to ask for one, a Jotform template, and Reddit and Facebook threads from teachers hunting for a free digital waiver. All of them stop at the wording. This page is for the studio that has the wording and needs every student signed before the mat goes down: a QR code at the door for first-timers, an assists answer the teacher sees on the roster, a class link that waits for the signature, and a new waiver version that reaches only the students who signed the old one. No legal advice: wording goes to the studio's own attorney, and the e-signature is a record of who signed what and when.
